newsitem.title: USA: Rain misses dry northwest Kansas, aids other wheat.
newsitem.headline: Rain misses dry northwest Kansas, aids other wheat.

text.p: Weekend rain largely missed the dry hard red winter wheat areas of northwest Kansas, while beneficial amounts of 0.3 to 1.0 inch fell across much of the the southern third of the state, meteorologists said.
"The heaviest thunderstorms were in the southern part," said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist. "As you move north the activity was much less."
Burgio said there were instances of quarter-inch rainfall in northwest Kansas, but the area was largely missed.
Rain and thunderstorms extended south into northwest and north central Oklahoma early Monday and were spreading into north Texas. By Tuesday, the Plains should turn dry for a few days, Burgio said.
"Thursday to Saturday we will see showers and thunderstorms for Texas, Oklahoma and eastern Kansas, possibly moderate amounts," he said.
Northwest Kansas could receive 0.1 to 0.5 inch, "with a slight chance for more," he said.

Fred Gesser, Weather Express Inc meteorologist, said the Thursday to Saturday storms may extend from Nebraska through Oklahoma, with the greatest rain amounts from Dodge City to Wichita in southwest to south central Kansas.
"It is kind of iffy in the west (Kansas)," he said.
Hard red winter wheat area high temperatures this week should be in the 80s degrees Fahrenheit in Kansas and Oklahoma, versus 90 degree weather this past weekend, said WSC'S Burgio.
